relevance.rationale: WRONG JOIN — THE MOST EXTREME IN THE SLICE. The seeded id names a single-author graduate textbook on general relativity issued by a university press in the 1980s. This PDF's front matter shows a single-author physics preprint arguing that entangled two- and three-qubit systems associate with 5+1 and 9+1 dimensional spacetimes reducing to 3+1 with a residual SU(3)×SU(2)×U(1)/Z₆ symmetry. Different author, different decade, different subject, different document type. The opaque filename gave the indexer nothing to work with. I set `id: null`; grep over references.ts finds no entry for this author, so no correct key exists. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE THREE CITATION SITES ON THE SEEDED ID: they become UNVERIFIED, not wrong. `MonoidalCalcVar.lean:41` cites 'Theorem 4.3.1'; `MonoidalCalcVar.lean:109` cites '§4.3 (Einstein)'; `GaugeTheory.lean:197` carries a bare pointer to references.ts. The textbook is not in uploads/ under any name, so I cannot confirm that those locators say what the sites claim. Verdict is `undetermined` because the DOCUMENT at this path cannot be assessed as a citation for that id at all — it is a different work. Separately: this preprint's own subject sits adjacent to the corpus's Standard-Model appendix and to the ℤ₆ compatibility relations of another entry in this same slice, so it may be worth triaging on its own merits — but I read only its abstract and introduction and will not assert relevance on that basis.

proposedActions.rationale: The join must be broken (id set to null here). Registering this preprint would require a relevance judgement I have not made, and the three locators on the seeded id cannot be checked without the textbook, which is not in uploads/.
